response.reason: The frozen acceptance and its bound candidate gates are sound, non-trivial, and correctly scope the completed-core Expand bug against the actual component subject. The acceptance starts a real isolated Next dev copy whose fixture page imports the real @/components/onboarding-checklist and supplies only source NAMES via sessionStorage/state (no replacement logic), so the component's own activeCount/requiredDone/allCoreActive/view computation is what is exercised. The base evidence is genuine and correctly negative: a fresh b2d0fe3 normal uv-sync clone produced 16 cases, 11 controls PASS, exactly 5 post-Expand heading failures (expand_core, expand_then_minimise, expand_source_transition, dismiss_after_override, storage_failure), 0 errors/skips, npm exit 0, owned deps/process groups/browser container removed, tracked source unchanged — and the negative is the missing 'Get started — connect your data sources' heading, never helper absence or an infra error. A trivial always-full fix cannot pass because auto_core/auto_all require the passive badge; a zero-helper inline fix cannot pass because the wiring mutant (checklistView override cleared) would leave all 16 green and the oracle requires a failing mutant. The unit gate pins the strict <7-day boundary (equality + 1ms either side), future/invalid/null/empty timestamps, required-vs-optional and duplicate progress counts, dismiss-wins-over-all, override-stays-full, and manual compact via 7 named Node tests, and its four closed fault wrappers (freshness/required/override/dismissal) must each fail with failureType:'testCodeFailure' (not import/parse). The portability repair installs the exact candidate package.json+package-lock.json via Node20 npm ci into owned scratch only when node_modules/next is absent, logs install output/exit, treats install failure/timeout as an infrastructure error (never a skip or semantic negative), and removes its npm group and scratch in finally; the install-failure and docker-timeout selftests prove these fail-closed paths. All six frozen artifact hashes and the proposal's embedded acceptance bytes match the bound sha256 values. The three prior sage blockers are repaired and falsifier-verified: version-only wrapper rejected under injected semantic faults (version-only-rejection.log), green wiring baseline fingerprint bound before worktree/Next allocation (stale-rejection.log), and post-creation Docker launch timeout handled with owner-verified container removal (docker-timeout-selftest.log). Real-page timestamp/role/past-asof/auth/accessibility, the 55 matched Playwright baselines, full make verify-fast, and the product-intention pass are explicitly and correctly deferred to separate mandatory checks rather than claimed by the component fixture. No real gap that would admit a false-positive or false-negative fix was found.
response.trivial_pass: Concrete trivial-pass attack: a candidate supplies a pytest 'wrapper' that merely invokes `node --version` (or asserts Node 20 is present) and returns pass, so the worker's Node unit tests never actually run and any semantic fault in the helper is invisible. Rejected: qualify_unit.py first runs the frozen 7-test contract against the real helper and asserts '# tests 7/# pass 7/# fail 0/# skipped 0/# todo 0', then injects each of the four bound fault wrappers (freshness equality-row re-add, required-counts-as-required, userExpanded-cleared, dismissed-cleared) into an OWNED checkout copy and requires the worker's wrapper to fail there with AssertionError/assert evidence and no import/parse/module-not-found error; a version-only wrapper yields 'worker wrapper did not reject freshness semantically', as captured in version-only-rejection.log. This same fault-injection also forces the worker's own Node unit tests (not the frozen contract alone) to be semantically meaningful.
checks: Actual component subject, not a replacement mock: the fixture page imports the real @/components/onboarding-checklist and only toggles source names via sessionStorage/useState; activeCount/requiredDone/requiredTotal/allCoreActive and the badge/full decision are computed inside the component.

True post-action awaits: every interaction uses `await click` followed by `await heading(p).waitFor`/`await waitText(...)` (3s timeouts) — no sleep-based settling; the five base failures are the awaited post-Expand heading locator timing out, matching the bug exactly.

Exact-16 no-skip population: main() re-parses the JUnit and asserts len(cases)==len(CASES) with the exact set of 16 test_onboarding[...] names and no skipped/failure/error; _observations also asserts set(result)==set(CASES).

Source fingerprint and immutability: snapshot() hashes every `git ls-files` tracked path (mode+sha256, symlink target as link) before and after, and both source-invariance.txt and outer-invariance.txt plus aggregate-errors.txt are asserted; the wiring probe additionally binds the baseline fingerprint (bytes, modes, symlinks) to the exact clean candidate before allocating any worktree or launching Next (stale-rejection.log).

Process-group cleanup: next/npm/browser procs are started with start_new_session=True and stop() killpg SIGTERM→SIGKILL with an absence-verified loop that raises if the owned group lingers; cleanup.txt records browser/Next/container absent.

Owner-Docker cleanup including launch timeout: select_browser labels the container hla-onboard.owner=<uuid>, and on TimeoutExpired writes partial stdout/stderr then the except path re-inspects the owner label before docker rm -f and verifies removal; docker-timeout-selftest.log proves post-creation timeout is surfaced with partial output retained and the owned container removed.

Unit contract correctness against source semantics: the 7 tests pin strict `<` 7 days (equality and 1ms either side), future-fresh, invalid/null/empty-not-fresh, duplicate-ignored required-vs-optional counts (activeCount=4/requiredDone=1/requiredTotal=2), allCoreActive via requiredDone>=requiredTotal, dismiss>override>compact/allCore precedence.

Meaningful mutation controls: four closed ESM fault wrappers import the exact helper by file URL and each must produce its specific `not ok N - <name>` with failureType:'testCodeFailure' (asserted non-zero exit and no ERR_MODULE/SyntaxError/Cannot find module), so infra failure cannot masquerade as a semantic negative.

Version-only wrapper rejected under real semantic faults (not just a node shim): qualify_unit.py runs the worker's wrapper against all four gate-generated faults in an owned copy and asserts AssertionError/assert evidence; version-only-rejection.log documents the rejection.

Production wiring is real, not a test artifact: run_wiring_probe copies the real helper byte-identically to a sidecar, substitutes a closed checklistView override, and the oracle requires a green 16-case baseline, exactly one changed tracked path (the helper), unchanged controls, and the same five post-Expand heading failures under the mutant; a candidate that does not consume checklistView would fail 'wiring mutant unexpectedly passed'.

Portability repair is fail-closed and preserves semantics: npm ci of the exact candidate package.json+package-lock.json into owned scratch only when modules absent, install exit/timeout logged, owned npm group stopped and scratch removed in finally; forced npm exit 72 surfaced as an infrastructure error (install-failure-selftest.log), never a skip or semantic negative, and the sixteen case/behavior strings are byte-identical to the prior packet.

Hash and artifact binding: the six frozen gate artifacts and the proposal's embedded acceptance bytes sha256 to the bound values (acceptance 70c99c10..., contract 0642c8ec..., qualify_unit 71d4827b..., qualify_wiring 07c5e86a..., run_wiring_probe d30353f6..., unit-gate-spec 97ff1eac...), and inventory.json covers 117 files.

Scope boundaries honored rather than waived: real-page timestamp/role/past-asof/auth/accessibility, the 55 matched Ubuntu Playwright baselines, full make verify-fast, train/dev/CI, and the product-intention pass against docs/product/core-household-operating-picture.md and docs/plans/kotona-operating-picture-brief.md are explicitly listed as separate mandatory later checks, not claimed by the component fixture.
